<objective>
Surface the duration half of TASK-05, which was specified, assumed by the tracer plan, and never built.

Purpose: `turns_used` is fully implemented and surfaced. Duration is not implemented anywhere —
`02-VERIFICATION.md` grepped the CLI, the HTTP layer, and the service layer and found no hits outside the
runner's internal `durationMs`, which never leaves `SpawnResult`. The task row already carries `started_at`
and `ended_at` as ISO timestamps, written through the single write path; nothing reads them back. This is
the one requirement in the phase whose `Pending` marker was always accurate.

The interesting part is not the subtraction, it is the boundary cases, and there are six of them: a run
under a second, a run still in flight, a task never dispatched, a clock that went backwards, a corrupt
timestamp, and a task the runner killed at its own wall-clock cap — the last of which only has an end
timestamp at all because `recordEvent` merges extra fields even for a transition it rejects. Each is a
different fact and each must be distinguishable; collapsing "not yet" into "zero" is the specific mistake
that would make a running task look instant.

Output: one pure function, one shaping function every taREDACTED_SECRET route passes through, and one CLI
column — with no new database column, so the derived value cannot drift from what it is derived from.
</objective>

  <behavior>
    - Started at a time and ended two seconds later: reports 2.
    - Started and ended 1999 milliseconds apart: reports 1 — truncated toward zero, never rounded up.
    - Started and ended 400 milliseconds apart: reports 0.
    - Started and ended at the identical timestamp: reports 0.
    - Started, not yet ended: reports no duration.
    - Neither started nor ended: reports no duration.
    - Ended without ever having started (a shape that should not occur, asserted anyway): reports no duration.
    - Ended one second BEFORE started, the clock-skew case: reports 0, never a negative number.
    - Either timestamp present but unparseable: reports no duration.
    - The shaping function returns every column of the task row unchanged, plus the derived duration under its own key — no column is dropped or renamed by passing through it.
  </behavior>
  <action>
Add two functions to `src/tasks/service.ts`, beside the existing pure resolvers rather than in a new module —
this file already owns `resolveModel`, `resolveCaps` and `resolveWallClockCapMs`, and a fourth pure helper
belongs with them rather than in a file of its own.

**`taskDurationSeconds(startedAt, endedAt)`** — a pure function taking the two nullable ISO strings and
returning a whole number of seconds or `null`. Parse both with `Date.parse`, and treat a `NaN` result the
same as an absent value: a corrupt row degrades to absent rather than to a confident wrong answer. Return
`null` unless BOTH parse to real times. Otherwise compute the millisecond delta, clamp a negative delta to
zero, and truncate toward zero to whole seconds. Truncation, not rounding, is the recorded reading of "in
seconds" from plan `02-04`'s flagged assumption, and this function is where that choice becomes a fact
rather than an assumption — say so in its doc comment, and say why the negative case is clamped rather than
returned: the timestamps are the persisted truth and a skewed clock is not licence to report a negative
elapsed time to an operator.

Be explicit in the doc comment about the distinction the `<behavior>` list turns on: `null` means "no
duration is knowable yet", `0` means "this ran, and it took under a second". Collapsing the two would make a
running task indistinguishable from an instant one, which is the one thing this value exists to tell an
operator apart.

**`toTaskRepresentation(row)`** — takes a task row and returns the wire shape: every column spread through
unchanged, plus a `durationSeconds` key holding the derived value. This exists so no route can carry the
field while another omits it. Adding the key here and not at each route is the whole design: the phase has
already shipped three primitives that existed at one layer and were never reached from another, and a
per-route spread is how a fourth would happen.

Do NOT add a duration column to the schema and do NOT persist the derived value. It is a pure function of
two columns that are already the single source of truth; a stored copy is a second source that can disagree
with the first, and no migration is worth buying that. Record this explicitly in `toTaskRepresentation`'s
doc comment so a later reader does not "optimise" it into a column.

**`src/tasks/service.test.ts`** — one `it.each` table driving `taskDurationSeconds` through all nine
`<behavior>` cases, plus a test that `toTaskRepresentation` preserves every key of the input row. Write
these before the implementation.
  </action>

## Artifacts this phase produces

**New symbols:** `taskDurationSeconds(startedAt, endedAt)` and `toTaskRepresentation(row)` in
`src/tasks/service.ts`.

**New wire field:** `durationSeconds` (integer seconds, or `null`) on the task representation returned by
`POST /tasks`, `GET /tasks`, `GET /tasks/:id`, and `POST /tasks/:id/cancel`.

**New CLI surface:** a `DURATION` column in `taskColumns`, rendered by `fleet task create|show|list|cancel`.

**Modified files:** `src/tasks/service.ts`, `src/tasks/service.test.ts`, `src/api/http/routes/tasks.ts`,
`src/api/http/routes/tasks.test.ts`, `src/cli/index.ts`, `src/cli/parity.test.ts`.

**Deliberately NOT produced:** no database column, no migration, no `drizzle/` file. The derived value is a
pure function of `started_at` and `ended_at`; persisting a copy would create a second source of truth that
can disagree with the first.

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| persisted ISO timestamps -> a derived number shown to an operator | A derivation that silently mishandles a boundary reports a confident wrong answer rather than failing |
| the daemon's own clock -> an elapsed-time claim | The two timestamps are written at different moments by different code paths; nothing guarantees monotonicity across a clock adjustment |
| a usage-proxy value -> an operator's mental model of subscription spend | A duration read as a cost figure misinforms the exact decision this project exists to inform |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-2-52 | Tampering | a negative or nonsensical duration from clock skew | medium | mitigate | `taskDurationSeconds` clamps a negative delta to zero and returns the absent value for any timestamp that does not parse; both cases are pinned by their own tests, and the raw ISO timestamps remain the untouched persisted truth |
| T-2-53 | Repudiation | a running task indistinguishable from an instant one | high | mitigate | The absent value and `0` are separate return values with separate tests and separate CLI glyphs; the acceptance criteria assert the not-yet case reports the absent value rather than zero, which is the specific collapse that would hide a stuck task |
| T-2-54 | Information Disclosure | duration read as a spend figure | medium | mitigate | D-29 already forbids persisting the CLI's imputed dollar figure; this plan adds no money-shaped sibling field, places duration beside turns as the paired usage proxy, and records the prohibition explicitly |
| T-2-55 | Tampering | a persisted duration drifting from its source timestamps | medium | mitigate | No column is added; the value is derived on every read. The acceptance criteria assert the schema file is unchanged and no migration file was created |
| T-2
